findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a sign-off worktree predates a sync-only merge into main.
Suppose G has green proof, HEAD branches from G with only Forge records, and main advances to C containing only exact sync output. The first iteration checks C against HEAD and returns here before reaching G. Older or absent generated files in HEAD fail the directional exact-output check described in src/forge/sync.py:453–456. Both G..main and G..HEAD satisfy the promised reuse conditions, but sign-off still demands another full run. Compare HEAD against the selected green commit rather than refusing against an intermediate commit without green proof. The new regression test misses this case because it always merges main into the sign-off worktree at tests/test_signoff_reuses_green_ancestor.py:51.

findings.title: Not done: Sign-off accepts the last green full run when every change since it is a Forge-written file or record, and a change to app code

why: Each merged repair makes the last green full run stale, so client sign-off waits about 30 minutes even for Forge-written bookkeeping changes. The review already runs after the green check in the sign-off path (src/forge/records.py decision_accept: the gaps list that includes the green check refuses before _signoff_review is called), so only the reuse part is new; the sign-off also checks green on the default branch's latest commit but reviews HEAD, and nothing ties the two together.
